chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Washshāʾ, from Aḥmad ibn ʿĀʾidh, from Abū Khadījah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I was with my father on the day in which he passed away, and he instructed me regarding matters of his ghusl, his shrouding, and his being entered into his grave. So I said: O my father, by Allah, since you fell ill I have not seen you in better condition than today; I do not see upon you the trace of death.
So he said: O my son, did you not hear ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام calling from behind the wall: O Muḥammad, come quickly!

key_terms.أَثَرَ الْمَوْتِ: the visible sign or trace of death
key_terms.غُسْلِهِ: his ghusl (ritual washing of the deceased)
key_terms.فَأَوْصَانِي: he instructed or bequeathed to me
key_terms.قُبِضَ: passed away; literally, his soul was taken
key_terms.كَفْنِهِ: his shrouding in the burial cloth

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show that the Imams عليهم السلام knew the time of their passing?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the final moments of an Imam, showing that he gave instructions concerning his burial rites while fully aware of his approaching death. It also indicates a hidden awareness and connection with the unseen, as he refers to the call of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام summoning him.
